claims.text: RabbitMQ stores a message's headers (set by the publisher) with it and delivers them to consumers; it does not create or rewrite a traceparent, though it may add its own x- headers (e.g. x-delivery-count on a quorum-queue redelivery).
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs 'Publishers' (message properties, headers), 'Quorum Queues' (x-delivery-count), 'Dead Letter Exchanges'

claims.text: Payment.TraceParent (payments.trace_parent) is set by RefundRequestedConsumer from its process span; RefundSender, a BackgroundService, starts 'refund attempt' from it and adds the result's outbox row inside it. Api outbox rows are made in a request or consumer span.

OutboxRelay can claim a row only after the transaction that inserted it has committed (uncommitted rows are not visible to its SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED); it claims rows on a 1-second PeriodicTimer tick.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs 'Transaction Isolation' (Read Committed sees only committed rows); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 DonHang.Messaging/OutboxRelay.cs lines 15, 21-24, 72-83

claims.text: Activity.Current flows with the async execution context; the relay's hosted-service loop does not run in the request's flow and starts no span of its own, so no span is current there.
claims.source_hint: .NET API docs System.Diagnostics.Activity.Current (AsyncLocal, flows across async calls); .NET docs 'Distributed tracing concepts'

claims.text: StartPublish calls StartChildOf(message.TraceParent, "publish <routing key>", Producer); StartChildOf parses the string with ActivityContext.TryParse(isRemote: true) and starts the activity from Đơn Hàng's ActivitySource with that context as parent.

In .NET a span is an Activity; ActivityKind Producer/Consumer mark the sending/receiving side; SetTag adds tags. StartActivity with an explicit parent ActivityContext uses its trace and parent ids; with default and none current it starts a new trace.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs 'Distributed tracing concepts' (Activity = span), ActivityKind enum, Activity.SetTag; ActivitySource.StartActivity(String, ActivityKind, ActivityContext, ...)

claims.text: OutboxRelay.RelayDueAsync starts MessageTracing.StartPublish for each message just before publisher.PublishAsync; RabbitMqPublisher puts the current span's traceparent (the publish span) in the message headers under 'traceparent'.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.Messaging/OutboxRelay.cs lines 53-61; DonHang.Messaging/RabbitMqPublisher.cs lines 30-35

claims.text: StartConsume reads the traceparent header from the delivery's IReadOnlyBasicProperties.Headers (Read) and starts a 'process <queue>' Consumer span under it; OrderEventsConsumer (Notifications), RefundRequestedConsumer (Payments), PaymentEventsConsumer (Api) call it.

A row with TraceParent null is still published; its publish span has no parent and starts a new trace, and the consumer's span joins that new trace (TracePropagationTests.ARowWithNoTraceParent_StartsANewTrace).

TracePropagationTests runs against real PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ containers and checks: the saved traceparent equals the request span's; the publish span's parent is the request span; the consumer span's parent is the publish span; one trace id.
Tempo groups spans by trace id, not by time; a trace has no end event and includes every span carrying its trace id, including spans started after the root span ended.
claims.source_hint: Grafana Tempo docs 'Introduction to tracing' (traces looked up by trace ID); OpenTelemetry spec 'Tracing API' (span parent/child, trace = set of spans sharing trace id)
